statements.subject: message
statements.description: The mail data may contain any of the 128 ASCII character codes, although experience has indicated that use of control characters other than SP, HT, CR, and LF may cause problems and SHOULD be avoided when possible.

statements.subject: smtp
statements.description: An extra <CRLF> MUST NOT be added, as that would cause an empty line to be added to the message.

statements.subject: smtp
statements.description: The only exception to this rule would arise if the message body were passed to the originating SMTP-sender with a final "line" that did not end in <CRLF>; in that case, the originating SMTP system MUST either reject the message as invalid or add <CRLF> in order to have the receiving SMTP server recognize the "end of data" condition.
actions: OR add <CRLF> to end of final message body line

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The custom of accepting lines ending only in <LF>, as a concession to non-conforming behavior on the part of some UNIX systems, has proven to cause more interoperability problems than it solves, and SMTP server systems MUST NOT do this, even in the name of improved robustness.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In particular, the sequence "<LF>.<LF>" (bare line feeds, without carriage returns) MUST NOT be treated as equivalent to <CRLF>.<CRLF> as the end of mail data indication.
actions: do not treat <LF>.<LF> as end-of-data indication

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the processing is successful, the receiver MUST send an OK reply.
statements.post_cond: OK_reply_sent = true & reverse_path_buffer.cleared = true & forward_path_buffer.cleared = true & mail_data_buffer.cleared = true

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the processing fails, the receiver MUST send a failure reply.
statements.post_cond: failure_reply_sent = true & reverse_path_buffer.cleared = true & forward_path_buffer.cleared = true & mail_data_buffer.cleared = true

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Errors that are diagnosed subsequently MUST be reported in a mail message, as discussed in Section 4.4.
actions: report error in a mail message
